byteHalf.why: Both halves are zlib.gzipSync totals read from files ON DISK over a clean build. They are load-independent and reproduce to the byte at every machine load this wave has seen.
byteHalf.buildTolerance: A MEASURED 10 B BAND across four independent builds on ZERO changed product bytes — the close recorded it as 2 B from two samples and this seat corrects it from four: 280,813 (unit a) · 280,811 (close) · 280,811 (CHECK 1) · 280,811 (repair build 1, this file's source, double-run identical) · 280,803 (repair build 2, taken after the §7 cadence destroyed dist/gh-pages — b-F6 confirmed a fourth time). Identical product bytes emit different chunk-hash TEXT, which compresses differently; raw is exactly stable at 886,610 B because the hashes are the same length. 10 B against a 5,909 B margin: immaterial to the verdict, material to the receipt, and stated rather than hidden. The gz delta is therefore -32,790 B within a +/-10 B build-drift band (extremes -32,788 B and -32,798 B).

cwvHalf.why: NOT-DIFFERENCEABLE at this bench. BEFORE.json's CWV half was taken at one machine load and this file's at two others; the halves differ by host load, not by the cure. The proof is internal to this wave: unit c's PRE-cure desktop p75 TBT was 58 ms and every POST-cure desktop reading (220 · 218 · 202 · 124 · 101 ms) is HIGHER, on a build that is 32,790 B gz LIGHTER. Publishing a 'delta' from those two halves would publish a fiction.
cwvHalf.whatIsPublishedInstead: Both halves are published WHOLE, each with its own load record, and DELTA.md states the non-differenceability with the measured reason and the named owner. The gate VERDICTS (G3 RED on mobile-4x, GREEN on desktop; G4 GREEN on both) are load-robust across all five sittings and ARE published as findings.
